Executive Order 5595. April 9 , 1931
Executive Order
The Honorable Nicholas Longworth
As a mark of respect to the memory of the Honorable Nicholas Longworth , late
Speaker and Member of the House of Representatives of the United States , it is
hereby ordered that the flags on the White House and public buildings in the District
of Columbia and the State of Ohio be placed at half mast to-day and on the day of the
funeral service at Cincinnati , Ohio, Saturday, April 11 , 1931 .
HERBERT HOOVER
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
April 9, 1931 .
[No. 5595]

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The complete original directs half-mast flags only on April 9 and April 11, 1931. The final prescribed day expires at its close; April 12 is the first civil date on which no part of the command remains due. This is a temporal limit in the command itself, not a performance deadline. The sole paragraph creates no independent continuing institution, payment, or delegated power.

Executive Order 5989. January 5, 1933
Executive Order
EXEMPTION OF DR. CHARLES ORRIN TOWNSEND FROM COMPULSORY
RETIREMENT FOR AGE
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 204 of Part II of the act
entitled " AN ACT Making appropriations for the Legislative Branch of the Govern-
ment for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1933, and for other purposes ," approved
June 30 , 1932 , Dr. Charles Orrin Townsend , Chief of the Sugar Division of the
United States Tariff Commission , who , during the current month, reaches the retire
ment age prescribed for automatic separation from the service , is hereby exempted
from the provisions of that section until January 31 , 1934.

June 30 , 1932 , Dr. Charles Orrin Townsend , Chief of the Sugar Division of the
United States Tariff Commission , who , during the current month, reaches the retire
ment age prescribed for automatic separation from the service , is hereby exempted

THE WHITE HOUSE ,
January 5, 1933 .
[No. 5989 ]

research_rationale:
The complete OFR original, printed pp. 1393-94 (PDF pp. 622-23), exempts Dr. Charles Orrin Townsend from section 204 compulsory retirement until January 31, 1934. This is an express terminal limit on the only prospective legal exemption. Under the owner's October 21 until-date ruling, January 31 is recorded inclusive; an exclusive reading at the start of January 31 remains an alternative for human review. No held instrument extends Townsend's exemption. The three number searches and held-person-name search report zero hits, with the OFR catalog's pre-1937 gap disclosed. The order creates no independent duty or delegated power.
